title: Annotatio I §.V: Bucer — Luther rejected our reading as if it removed presence; nostri deny absence-sign
pass_a_gloss: But that Luther, he says, rejected our people’s interpretation — so far as I can judge from his writings — came about because he judged that by it Christ’s presence in the Supper was taken away and removed. Our people, however, by no means say that the bread is that kind of sign of Christ’s body by which Christ’s body is denoted to be absent or not taken — which they have made known hitherto by many published writings.
pass_b_english: Bucer: Luther rejected our interpretation, so far as his writings show, because he thought it removed Christ’s presence from the Supper.
Our doctors deny that bread is a sign meaning the body is absent or not taken — and they have said so in many books.
source_text: Quòd verò Lutherus, inquit, nostrorum interpretationem rejecit, ex eo, quantum ego quidem ex scriptis ejus judicare possum, factum est, quòd praesentiam Christi per eam in Coena tolli & removeri fuit arbitratus. Nostri vero panem ejusmodi signum corporis Christi nequaquam esse dicunt, per quod corpus Christi abesse vel non sumi denotetur, id quod multis scriptis editis hactenus notum fecerunt.

lemmas.gloss: to be absent or not taken

choices.english: be absent or not be taken

notes: Luther feared absence; nostri deny absence-sign.
